_readme: HAND-LABELLED GROUND TRUTH FOR FORM CLASSIFICATION.
The question for each (record, form) pair: is the document ABOUT this form —
revising it, changing its fee or edition, changing how it is filed — or does
it merely name it? A filter that returns every document containing the string
'I-129' is not a filter anyone can monitor on.
HOW THE POOL WAS DRAWN, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE CLASSIFIER'S OUTPUT.
Candidates come from the DOCUMENTS, not from what the classifier claimed.
Full Federal Register texts were fetched for all 348 records that have one,
and every record whose title, abstract or body names the value became a
candidate. Scoring against your own output can only measure precision, and
it measures it against the thing being tested.
Each judgement was made from the document's own words — title, abstract, and
the body passages containing the mention — with the deciding span quoted. The
annotator was not shown what the classifier decided.
THE HOLDOUT. Every record carries a `holdout` flag, set by hashing its id, so
the split is stable and independent of both content and classifier answer.
Nothing may be tuned against the holdout half. It exists to catch the
overfitting that fixing a classifier against its own benchmark produces.
NOT INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED. The reviewers for this dimension did not run to
completion, so all but one of these labels carry a single annotator's
judgement rather than two. That is a weaker basis than the H-1B and country
sets and it is stated here rather than left for someone to discover.
`onlyInBody` is the field that answers a specific question: can an archive
that keeps only titles and abstracts see this at all? For 82 of the 121
documents genuinely about a form, the answer is no.

pairs.quote: Extension, Without Change, of a Currently Approved Collection: Form No. I-352; Immigration Bond
pairs.why: The title is the PRA collection notice for this form, and the body identifies it as the collection at issue: '(3) Agency form number, if any ...: I-352; U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.' A PRA notice about a form is about that form. The body also describes the filing mechanics — bonds submitted 'electronically through ICE's eBonds system which encompasses the I-352, while individuals are still required to complete the bond form manually.'

pairs.quote: USCIS Changes Validity Period for Any Form I-693 Signed on or after Nov. 1, 2023
pairs.why: The document changes the validity rule for the form itself: 'a Form I-693 ... signed by a civil surgeon on or after Nov. 1, 2023, is only valid while the application the Form I-693 was submitted with is pending.' That governs when the form may be submitted and when a resubmission is required.

pairs.quote: USCIS is changing how we process Form N-648 by focusing greater attention on the veracity of medical certifications
pairs.why: The abstract states the guidance changes the processing and review of this specific form, which is a change to how the form is adjudicated and what scrutiny its certification must survive — not a passing reference.

pairs.quote: USCIS is waiving any and all requirements that applicants for adjustment of status ... present documentation on their Form I-693, Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, that they received the COVID-19 vaccination
pairs.why: The waiver changes what must be documented on the form, which is squarely 'changes what must be submitted with it' — the content of the I-693 itself is altered for these applicants.

pairs.quote: the transition from accepting paper-based forms of payment to accepting only credit or debit cards and the new Authorization for ACH Transactions (Form G-1650)
pairs.why: The guidance introduces this form as new and makes it the vehicle for ACH fee payment effective October 28, 2025. Creating a form and setting when it is used is as direct a subject relationship as revising one.

pairs.quote: Extension, Without Change, of a Currently Approved Collection: Form No. I-901; Fee Remittance for Certain F, J and M Nonimmigrants
pairs.why: A Paperwork Reduction Act extension notice for this collection; the body names it as the agency form number for the collection — 'Form I-901; U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement' — and describes its function, 'SEVP used the Form I-901 ... to provide a receipt to the F, J, or M nonimmigrant upon payment.'

pairs.quote: Revised Guidance for Form N-648 Submission and Review Process
pairs.why: The title states the guidance revises the submission and review process for this form, and the abstract confirms USCIS 'is changing how the Medical Certification for Disability Exceptions ( Form N-648 ) is processed.' That changes how the form is filed and reviewed.

pairs.quote: This update involves the publication of two new forms, the Authorization for ACH Transactions ( Form G-1650 ) and Exemption for Paper Fee Payment ( Form G-1651 )
pairs.why: The update publishes this form as one of two new forms and puts it into effect October 28, 2025. Publishing a form is a change to the form, not a mention of it.

pairs.quote: the publication of two new forms, the Authorization for ACH Transactions ( Form G-1650 ) and Exemption for Paper Fee Payment ( Form G-1651 )
pairs.why: Same sentence establishes this form as newly published by this update and effective October 28, 2025 — the document creates it rather than citing it.

pairs.quote: In accordance with HR-1, the existing fee for Form I-94 Arrival/Departure Record applications will not change for FY 2026.
pairs.why: The I-94 fee is one of the fees this notice adjusts for inflation, not background: the body devotes section II.B to it — 'Section II.B. explains the inflation adjustment formula for the HR-1 I-94 fee and details why, upon applying the inflation adjustment formula and rounding down to the nearest dollar, the fee amount will not increase in FY 2026' — and the published fee table carries a line for 'Application for CBP Form I-94 at land border ports of entry.' The document sets the FY 2026 amount for this form's fee; the outcome happening to be zero change does not make the mention incidental.

pairs.quote: H-1B Final Rule, H-2 Final Rule, and Revised Form I-129 Effective Jan. 17, 2025
pairs.why: The title announces a revised edition of the form taking effect on a stated date. A revision with an effective date is a change to the form itself, not a passing reference.

pairs.quote: Form Number: I-775. Current Actions: Revision. Type of Review: Revision.
pairs.why: PRA notice revising this collection, and the body states a substantive change to how it is submitted: 'The requirement to submit original documents bearing original signatures of company representatives, was modified to include electronic transfer of CBP Form I-775'.

pairs.quote: DHS proposes to adjust the fees that U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) charges for Form N-400, and Form N-336, to end both the reduced fee option for Form N-400
pairs.why: The rule adjusts this form's fee, removes its reduced fee option, and ends fee waiver eligibility for it. A direct fee change.

pairs.quote: the availability of fee waivers for both forms
pairs.why: Named alongside N-400 throughout as a form whose fee is adjusted and whose fee waiver eligibility ends; body confirms 'A. Full Cost Recovery for Form N-400 and Form N-336 Fees'.

pairs.quote: See USCIS, Form G-1055, ``Fee Schedule,''
pairs.why: Appears once inside a footnote citation supporting the current fee figures. Background reference; the rule does not change G-1055.

pairs.quote: I. Paperwork Reduction Act 1. USCIS Form I-912 2. USCIS Form N-336 3. USCIS Form N-400
pairs.why: The rule's Paperwork Reduction Act section carries a dedicated subsection for this form, in parallel with the two forms that are indisputably the rule's subject, which indicates its information collection is addressed by the rule. TORN: the only supporting text is a table-of-contents heading; no supplied passage states what changes for I-912, so this label rests on document structure rather than on an operative sentence.

pairs.quote: which covers Forms ETA-9142B, Appendices A, B, C, and D, ETA-9142B, Final Determination, H-2B Seafood Industry Attestation, and related form instructions. This action seeks to renew these forms.
pairs.why: A PRA information collection request that renews this form and its appendices and instructions. A PRA notice about a form is about that form.

pairs.quote: The Department also proposes to eliminate the Form ETA-9155, H-2B Registration and pertinent instructions, as employers are not required to complete and submit this form.
pairs.why: The document proposes to eliminate this form, its instructions, and its burden estimates. Eliminating a form is the strongest possible form of concerning it.

pairs.quote: the Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record ( Form I-693 ) is generally valid only for the immigration benefit application for which it was submitted
pairs.why: The alert changes the policy governing this form's validity and reuse, which changes when it must be resubmitted. The form is the named subject of both title and abstract.

pairs.quote: such as the Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status ( Form I-485 )
pairs.why: Introduced by 'such as' as one example of a benefit application to which an I-693 may be tied. The alert's operative change is to I-693 validity, not to I-485. TORN: a reader could argue the policy changes what must accompany an I-485; I resolved against the match because the only quotable span frames I-485 as an example.

pairs.quote: will publish revised editions of Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status
pairs.why: New edition published, older editions rejected starting a stated date. An edition change is squarely a change to the form.

pairs.quote: and Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (edition date for both: 09/15/26)
pairs.why: Same announcement gives this form a new edition date and rejects older editions; the abstract states both were 'revised to align with' a final rule.

pairs.quote: providing updated procedures for submitting a Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers, accompanied by a permanent labor certification
pairs.why: Updates the procedures for submitting the form and what must accompany it. Both are explicit isSubject criteria.

pairs.quote: the new Form I-94 fee requirement
pairs.why: The IFR codifies a new minimum fee for applications for this record and specifies it cannot be waived or reduced. A direct fee change.

pairs.quote: the retention of the Form I-589 filing fee for every application
pairs.why: Codifies that the asylum filing fee is retained by USCIS if the form is rejected, and codifies the asylum and annual asylum fees. A change to the form's fee treatment.

pairs.quote: Establishes a fee requirement that, for USCIS, is applicable to the filing of Form I-102, Application for Replacement/Initial No
pairs.why: The new statutory fee is stated to attach to the filing of this specific form, which changes the cost of filing it. Not a passing example; it is how the rule operationalizes the I-94 fee at USCIS.

pairs.quote: Form Number: I-736. Current Actions: Revision.
pairs.why: PRA revision of this collection that changes how it is filed: 'CBP intends to migrate from paper I-736 to a mandatory automated environment; therefore, the collection of a paper form will no longer be acceptable.'

pairs.quote: is announcing updated procedures for submitting a Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers, accompanied by a permanent labor certification approval
pairs.why: Changes how the petition is filed and what documentation must be submitted with it. Named in title and abstract as the notice's subject.

pairs.quote: DOL sent an original approved Form ETA-9089, Application for Permanent Employment Certification, and final determination and letter to the employer
pairs.why: Every supplied mention is past-tense background describing the pre-FLAG process ('DOL sent...', 'the employer was required to sign and retain...'). The notice changes the I-140 submission requirement, not the ETA-9089 form. TORN: the title's 'Permanent Labor Certification Final Determination' is the ETA-9089 output, so a reader could argue this touches ETA-9089 filings; I resolved against the match because no supplied span states a change to that form.

pairs.quote: had to submit an uncertified Form ETA-750B (now discontinued)
pairs.why: Named once, in the past tense, and expressly identified as discontinued. Pure background about superseded practice.

pairs.quote: update the maximum validity periods for Employment Authorization Documents (EADs, Form I-766) for certain EAD categories
pairs.why: The guidance acts directly on this form: it sets how long the document USCIS issues on Form I-766 remains valid, with a stated effective date. The form is the thing being changed, not an example or citation.

pairs.quote: USCIS will publish a revised edition of Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status (edition date: 09/18/26)
pairs.why: The document's entire purpose is a new edition of this form and the rejection of older editions. That is squarely an edition change to Form I-485.

pairs.quote: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) will require aliens to pay a new fee to apply for a CBP Form I-94 Arrival/Departure Record
pairs.why: The notice sets the fee that must be paid to apply for the form, and the body states the resulting total: 'the total fee for aliens who apply for a CBP Form I-94 (i.e., aliens arriving at a land border port of entry) will be $30'. A fee change for the form is squarely isSubject.

pairs.quote: clarify the interview criteria for aliens who are asylees and refugees and their derivative family members filing Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status
pairs.why: The form is the object of the policy change, not a passing example: the update defines who among I-485 filers must be interviewed, which changes what an I-485 applicant must go through on that application. I note the tension that an interview-criteria change is not literally one of the enumerated triggers (revision, edition, fee, filing mechanics, required evidence); I still call it isSubject because the form is the document's stated subject rather than background.

pairs.quote: Title: Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Information (Form I-736). OMB Number: 1651-0109. Form Number: I-736. Current Actions: Revision.
pairs.why: A Paperwork Reduction Act notice about the form, explicitly a 'Revision', and the body also changes how it is filed: 'CBP intends to migrate from paper I-736 to a mandatory automated environment; therefore, the collection of a paper form will no longer be acceptable.'

pairs.quote: DHS proposes to increase the fee for adjudicating Form I-246, Application for a Stay of Deportation or Removal, from $155 to $755.
pairs.why: An explicit fee change for the named form; the form is in the title, abstract, and throughout the body.

pairs.quote: Title: Visa Waiver Signatory Carrier Program (Form I-775). OMB Number: 1651-0110. Form Number: I-775. Current Actions: Revision.
pairs.why: A PRA notice revising this collection, and the body changes how the form may be submitted: 'CBP would like to make the electronic submission and approval of this information permanent.'

pairs.quote: Agency Information Collection Activities; Extension, Without Change, of a Currently Approved Collection: Form No. I-901; Fee Remittance for Certain F, J and M Nonimmigrants
pairs.why: A Paperwork Reduction Act notice whose collection is this form; the body confirms 'Agency form number, if any... Form I-901'. An extension without change is still a PRA action about the form.

pairs.quote: This IFR amends DHS regulations to end the practice of automatically extending the validity of employment authorization documents (Forms I-766 or EADs)
pairs.why: The rule changes the validity period of the I-766 document itself — that is the operative action of the rule, and the form is named in the abstract.

pairs.quote: There are several employment-eligible categories that are not included in DHS regulations but instead are described in the form instructions to Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (EAD application).
pairs.why: Genuinely torn. The rule plainly affects people who file an I-765 renewal, since the automatic extension that attached to a timely-filed renewal is being removed. But every span that actually names I-765 is background or a footnote citation to the form instructions ('which they do by filing a Form I-765 Application for Employment Authorization, in order to receive a Form I-766 EAD'); nothing in the text given revises I-765, changes its fee, or changes how it is filed. Following the rule to prefer negative when torn, and because I cannot quote a span where the document acts on I-765, I label it false.

pairs.quote: These aliens are issued an Arrival-Departure Record (Form I-94) indicating their employment-authorized status in the United States
pairs.why: Pure background, explaining a class of aliens who do not file separate employment-authorization requests. The rule does nothing to Form I-94.

pairs.quote: 4. I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification
pairs.why: Appears only as a background section heading in the rule's table of contents. Mildly torn on whether this string is even a form reference rather than a topic heading; either way the document takes no action on Form I-9, so false.

pairs.quote: Extension Package for Form ETA-9089, Application for Permanent Employment Certification, and Appendices
pairs.why: A PRA information collection request covering this form and its appendices: 'DOL seeks to extend, without changes, the validity of Form ETA-9089, Application for Permanent Employment Certification'. A PRA notice about a form is about that form.

pairs.quote: which covers Forms ETA-9141, Application for Prevailing Wage Determination; Form ETA-9141, General Instructions; Form ETA-9141, Appendix A, Request for Additional Worksite(s)
pairs.why: A PRA extension request whose collection is this form: 'This action seeks to extend the forms without changes.' A PRA notice about a form is about that form.

pairs.quote: Form ETA 9165, Employer-Provided Survey Attestations to Accompany H-2B Prevailing Wage Determination Request Based on a Non-OEWS Survey; and Form ETA-9165, General Instructions. This action seeks to extend the forms without changes.
pairs.why: The same PRA extension covers this form as a named component of OMB Control Number 1205-0508, not as a passing example.

pairs.quote: such applicants do not need to file a Confirmation of Valid Job Offer or Request for Job Portability Under INA Section 204(j) ( Form I-485, Supplement J ) if they change jobs
pairs.why: The update changes whether this form must be filed at all for a class of applicants. That is a direct change to what must be submitted.

pairs.quote: adjustment applicants whose immigrant petitions are based on a national interest waiver are eligible for portability under the American Competitiveness in the Twenty-First Century Act of 2000 (AC21)
pairs.why: Somewhat torn. The literal string 'I-485' occurs only inside the name 'Form I-485, Supplement J', so one could argue the base form is never independently mentioned. I still label it true because Supplement J is a supplement to Form I-485, the population addressed is adjustment (I-485) applicants, and the update changes what those applicants must file with their adjustment application.

pairs.quote: Because the IFR provides that failure to pay the Annual Asylum Fee (AAF) results in rejection of the pending Form I-589, DHS is adding ``rejected'' to the 8 CFR 208.7(a)(1)(v) language so that the regulation expressly covers both denials and rejections of asylum applications.
pairs.why: This is the correction's own operative change, and it is framed around the consequence for a pending Form I-589. The abstract independently ties the corrected IFR to 'the retention of the Form I-589 filing fee for every application'.

pairs.quote: The IFR codified certain immigration fees and other provisions required by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1) and amended USCIS regulations governing asylum and annual asylum fees, the new Form I-94 fee requirement
pairs.why: Torn. Form I-94 is named in the abstract, not merely the body, and the rule being corrected did change the I-94 fee. But this document is only a correction, and every I-94 mention describes the earlier IFR's scope as background; the sole change it makes, quotable in the body, is the asylum 'rejected' language in 8 CFR 208.7(a)(1)(v). Nothing in the text given shows this correction touching the I-94 provisions, so following the prefer-negative rule I label it false.

pairs.quote: unfair documentary practices during the employment eligibility verification process (Form I-9 and E-Verify)
pairs.why: Named only to describe the category of discrimination IER handles. The collection being revised is the IER charge form; nothing in the text revises Form I-9, its edition, its fee, or how it is filed.

pairs.quote: E-Verify+ was developed as a demonstration project to further integrate the Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification, process with the E-Verify electronic employment eligibility confirmation process
pairs.why: The collection being extended is E-Verify+, not the I-9 collection. I was genuinely torn because E-Verify+ absorbs the I-9 process, so an I-9 watcher might want it — but the text says the extension is 'Without Change' and never states that Form I-9, its edition, or its filing changes. Going negative per the tie-break rule.

pairs.quote: Specifically, the Form I-129 requires the employer to provide the names and addresses of all agents, facilitators, staff, recruiters
pairs.why: Cited as an existing USCIS requirement, used as background justification for rescinding DOL's own recruiter-disclosure provision. DOL is not amending Form I-129 and nothing here changes how it is filed. This is exactly the 'names I-129 in passing' case the filter must exclude.

pairs.quote: unless a specific exemption applies, a copy of Form ETA-790/790A, submitted as set forth in Sec. 655.121(a)
pairs.why: Appears inside recited filing requirements for the Application for Temporary Employment Certification. I was torn: this is regulatory filing text in a rule that amends those sections, so it could be amendatory rather than merely restated — but the quoted words alone do not show any change to the ETA-790/790A requirement, so I cannot defend a positive from the document's own words.

pairs.quote: Programs Affected, OMB Control Numbers <bullet> OMB No. 1615-0052--Form N-400, Application for Naturalization
pairs.why: Listed as a program affected by the new collection, with its own burden estimate ('the information collection N-400 is 909,700'). A PRA collection that adds identifiers to this form is about this form.

pairs.quote: OMB No. 1615-0013--Form I-131, Application for Travel Document
pairs.why: Named in the 'Programs Affected' list and given its own respondent/burden estimate, so the new identifier collection changes what this form gathers.

pairs.quote: OMB No. 1615-0017--Form I-192, Application for Advance Permission to Enter as a Nonimmigrant
pairs.why: Listed as affected, with an explicit burden estimate ('the information collection I-192 is 68,050').

pairs.quote: OMB No. 1615-0023--Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status
pairs.why: Listed as affected by the new generic clearance, with a respondent count of 1,060,585 in the burden section.

pairs.quote: OMB No. 1615-0067--Form I-589, Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal
pairs.why: Listed as affected, with an explicit burden estimate ('the information collection I-589 is 203,379').

pairs.quote: OMB No. 1615-0068--Form I-590, Registration for Classification as Refugee
pairs.why: Listed as affected, with a burden estimate ('I-590 is 53,100').

pairs.quote: OMB No. 1615-0037--Form I-730, Refugee/Asylee Relative Petition
pairs.why: Listed as affected, with a burden estimate ('the information collection I-730 is 13,000').

pairs.quote: OMB No. 1615-0038--Form I-751, Petition to Remove Conditions on Residence
pairs.why: Listed as affected, and named again in the burden section ('the information collection I-751').

pairs.quote: OMB No. 1615-0045--Form I-829, Petition by Investor to Remove Conditions on Permanent Resident Status
pairs.why: Listed under 'Programs Affected' for the new collection. No burden estimate appears in the supplied passages, but the affected-programs listing alone shows the collection reaches this form.

pairs.quote: Agency form number, if any, and the applicable component of the DHS sponsoring the collection: N-648; USCIS
pairs.why: This is the form being revised: it is the designated agency form number for the collection, and the notice gives N-648 respondent counts and hour burdens for both the medical professional and the applicant.

pairs.quote: the doctor states that an applicant filing an Application for Naturalization, Form N-400, is unable to complete the English
pairs.why: Named only to identify whose naturalization application the N-648 certification supports. The revision is to N-648; nothing here changes Form N-400, its edition, its fee, or its filing.

pairs.quote: In 8 CFR 264.1(a) and (b), DHS is adding Form I-94A/94W to the item for the Form I-94
pairs.why: The rule updates the I-94 entry itself — the section heading is 'Updating Form I-94 as Evidence of Registration' and the rule revises the classes of aliens for whom an I-94 constitutes evidence of registration.

pairs.quote: DHS is adding Form I-94A/94W to the item for the Form I-94
pairs.why: Added by this rule to the 8 CFR 264.1(a) and (b) tables as evidence of registration — a direct change to the form's regulatory status.

pairs.quote: the table of 8 CFR 264.1(b) the USCIS Proof of Alien G-325R Registration
pairs.why: Added by this rule to the 8 CFR 264.1(b) table; the rule's whole subject is designating the registration form and its evidence.

pairs.quote: Revising the table in 8 CFR 264.1(a) by removing the entries related to the I-67, Inspection Record--Hungarian refugees
pairs.why: The rule removes this form's entry from the registration table — an action on the form, not a mention of it.

pairs.quote: removing the entries related to the I-67, Inspection Record--Hungarian refugees (Act of July 25, 1958), I-691, Notice of Approval for Status as a Temporary Resident
pairs.why: Its entry is being removed from 8 CFR 264.1(a) by this rule, ending its status as prescribed evidence of registration.

pairs.quote: I-691, Notice of Approval for Status as a Temporary Resident, and I-700, Application for Status
pairs.why: Named in the same amendatory bullet removing entries from the 8 CFR 264.1(a) table.

pairs.quote: Revising the table in 8 CFR 264.1(a) by updating the entry relating to Form I-181, Memorandum of Creation of Record of Lawful Permanent Residence
pairs.why: The rule revises this form's table entry and the class of aliens it covers.

pairs.quote: Revising the table in 8 CFR 264.1(a) by updating the entry relating to Form I-485 and the Adjustment of Status Form Title
pairs.why: The rule revises the form title carried for I-485 in 8 CFR 264.1(a) — a direct change to how the form is described in regulation.

pairs.quote: DHS is revising the form title and class of alien of Form I-590
pairs.why: Explicit amendatory action on this form's title and covered class.

pairs.quote: updating the entry relating to Form I-817, Application for Voluntary Departure under the Family Unity Program
pairs.why: The rule revises the form title of I-817 in 8 CFR 264.1(a).

pairs.quote: $500 fee for first-time applicants filing Form I-821, Application for Temporary Protected Status, not including the $30 biometric services fee
pairs.why: The notice adjusts this fee — the table carries an 'I-821 TPS Fee' row with the pre- and post-adjustment amounts (500 to 510).

pairs.quote: $250 fee for any alien who files Form I-360
pairs.why: Its fee is adjusted here; the table includes an 'I-360 Special Immigrant Juvenile (SIJ) Fee' row with the adjustment computation.

pairs.quote: I-589 Asylum Fee (Initial fee for aliens $100 2.70 $2.70 $102.70
pairs.why: Two I-589 fee rows (initial asylum fee and annual pending asylum application fee) are given adjusted amounts in the notice's fee table.

pairs.quote: I-765 Initial Asylum Applicant Employment 550 2.70 14.88 564.88 560
pairs.why: Six I-765 EAD fee rows (asylum, parole, TPS; initial and renewal) receive adjusted amounts in the table.

pairs.quote: I-131 EAD upon new period of Parole (Re- 275 2.70 7.44 282.44 280
pairs.why: The table sets an adjusted fee for the I-131 re-parole EAD, so this notice changes an I-131 fee.

pairs.quote: by section 100008 from any alien who submits an application for a Form I-94 Arrival/ Departure Record, will be adjusted for inflation as required by the law in a subsequent notice in the Federal Register
pairs.why: The notice expressly says the I-94 fee will be adjusted in a SUBSEQUENT notice, so this document does not change it. I was torn because the same statutory fee regime covers I-94 and a fee watcher would find it relevant, but the text affirmatively excludes I-94 from this adjustment.

pairs.quote: Type of Request: Revision of a Currently Approved Collection. Originating Office: Bureau of Consular Affairs, Visa Office. Form Number: DS-3035
pairs.why: DS-3035 is the form number of the collection being revised; the notice describes its content, respondents, and the electronic submission method ('Applicants will complete and submit the DS-3035 electronically at the J Visa Waiver Online portal').

pairs.quote: the alien filed a Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, that is postmarked or electronically filed as of December 15, 2025 that is still pending
pairs.why: Named as a condition under which an individual's parole is spared from termination. I was somewhat torn because a filing date cutoff matters to I-485 filers, but the notice does not change Form I-485, its fee, its contents, or how or where it is filed.

pairs.quote: The modernized FRP programs were available by invitation only to certain petitioners with approved Forms I-130, Petition for Alien Relative
pairs.why: Background describing how the terminated programs selected participants, plus discussion of the limits of relying on an approved I-130 during vetting. Nothing changes the form itself.

pairs.quote: the process was changed for new filings in August 2023 to adopt use of the online Form I-134A
pairs.why: Appears in footnoted historical background on the terminated programs' mechanics. I was torn because ending those programs ends a use of the I-134A, but the text never says the form, its filing, or its contents change.

pairs.quote: The FRP programs created in 2007, for Cuba, and 2014, for Haiti, utilized Form I-131, Application for Travel Documents, Parole Documents, and Arrival/Departure Records, to request parole from USCIS
pairs.why: Purely historical description of how the legacy CFRP and HFRP programs were once filed; the notice makes no change to Form I-131.

pairs.quote: Agency form number, if any, and the applicable component of the DHS sponsoring the collection: G-1592; USCIS
pairs.why: G-1592 is the agency form number for the collection this PRA notice extends, so the notice is about that form even though the extension is without change.

pairs.quote: Agency form number, if any, and the applicable component of the DHS sponsoring the collection: I-912; USCIS

contested.reviewerSays: The quote shows the document scoping and motivating itself with the I-94, not acting on it. Half one, "aliens subject to Form I-94 (Arrival/Departure Record) requirements," uses the existing and unchanged I-94 requirement to define who may participate — a population definition, the archetypal scoping citation, where the form identifies the class rather than being the object acted upon. Half two, "to further automate the I-94 process," is a purpose clause about a program broader than this pilot, and the body the annotator cites confirms it: "CBP is also now working to fully automate all I-94 processes. CBP has already automated the I-94 process for air and sea travel with a commercial carrier." The word "further" and the phrase "already automated" mark that as a status report on a continuing multi-year initiative that predates and outlives this notice — the same background-prose pattern docs/who-is-affected.md rules out for countries. Everything the notice actually does is biometric: collect facial images, test the technology's effectiveness, feed the entry-exit system, address privacy. The I-94's content, issuance, requirements, exemptions (8 CFR 235.1(h)), and filing are all untouched, and participation is voluntary and time-limited, so a person holding an I-94 who does nothing is in exactly the position they were in before. The annotator concedes this ("the notice amends no I-94 requirement and the form itself is untouched"), which under the stated standard is the answer. The nearest thing to action on the form is an added voluntary channel for reporting departure alongside the existing practice of returning a printed I-94 to CBSA at the northern border — and the notice describes that practice as pre-existing background as well. Contrast the codebase's own benchmark in forms.ts: a PRA notice is by definition about a specific form; this is a pilot-program notice in which the I-94 is the record system the pilot's data feeds, which is a relationship of context, not of subject. Recurrence alone (eight body passages) is frequency, not aboutness.
